title: The Last Bus
stanzas: The timetable said 11:40.
By midnight the glass case had fogged
and the only other person at the stop
had folded his jacket into a pillow.
Across the road, a shuttered pharmacy,
a dog working the bins without hurry,
and the sea somewhere behind the buildings,
turning its stones over and over.
The bus came late and half-lit.
The driver counted coins with one hand
and let me on without asking,
as though I had been expected.
I sat where the heater had been.
The town gave up its streets one by one—
the chai stall, the tyre shop, the school gate—
until there was only the road and rain on it.
Someone had scratched two names in the window
and a date gone soft with weather.
I put my hand over them the way you cover
a candle when the wind gets in.
